items.stem: What is a primary benefit of routing all AI calls through a gateway?

options.text: Central control of routing, budgets, policy and observability across providers
options.rationale: Correct: a gateway centralises cross-cutting controls instead of duplicating them.
A gateway does not remove provider costs.

options.text: It guarantees the model never makes mistakes
options.rationale: A gateway does not change model accuracy.

options.text: It eliminates the need for any monitoring
options.rationale: A gateway is where monitoring is centralised, not removed.

items.explanation: Correct: a gateway centralises cross-cutting controls instead of duplicating them.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO keep one tenant from exhausting shared AI spend? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: a budget caps how much a tenant can spend.

options.text: Rate limits and quotas per API key
options.rationale: Correct: rate limits and quotas bound usage over time.

options.text: A single shared unlimited key for everyone
options.rationale: An unlimited shared key allows runaway spend.
Without tracking you cannot enforce or see spend.

items.explanation: Correct: a budget caps how much a tenant can spend.

items.stem: A provider starts returning errors. What should a production AI gateway do?

options.text: Fall back to an alternate provider or model and retry within limits
options.rationale: Correct: routing with fallbacks keeps the service up when one provider fails.

options.text: Return the error to every user and stop
options.rationale: A single provider outage should not take the whole service down.

options.text: Retry the failing provider forever with no limit
options.rationale: Unbounded retries amplify the outage and cost.
Turning off the gateway removes exactly the control that handles this.

items.explanation: Correct: routing with fallbacks keeps the service up when one provider fails.
